newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. bank grants Algeria $150 mln for oil sector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank grants Algeria $150 mln for oil sector.

text.p: The U.S. Eximbank lent $150 million to Algeria's state-owned oil and gas firm Sonatrach to finance the upgrading of oil and gas facilities, the Algerian official news agency APS said on Tuesday.
The deal was signed on Monday in Washington at the headquarters of the Eximbank, the U.S. government financing arm to enhance U.S. exports.
"This accord will help the Americans investing in Algeria and we hope it will be followed by more accords soon," Sonatrach's finance department head Ahmed Mostefaoui said at the signing ceremony.
The loan was granted at a 6.64 percent interest rate, lower than the 10 percent rate offered by European banks, it said.
APS said the loan was signed before a visit by former Defence Secretary Dick Cheney to Algeria. It gave no date.
Cheney is the current chairman and chief executive officer of Halliburton Co, the agency said.
U.S.-based firms Halliburton and Anadarko Petroleum Corp signed in September a $177 million agreement with Sonatrach to develop the southern field of Hassi Berkine located in south Algeria.
Sonatrach and Anakarko, linked by a production sharing deal, discovered the field in the southern basin of Ghadames, in the Sahara, where 34 of Algeria's 207 discoveries lie.
The value of Algeria's exports of oil and gas rose to $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from the year before.
